text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An ailing Koigi wa Wamwere is released on a 200,000 shilling bond to enable him to receive medical treatment in Britain pending appeal.
- Part of Kenyan air space is closed for a while following difficulties encountered with a contingency plan put in place to respond to a go-slow by air traffic controllers.
- Eight armed and drunk Criminal Investigation Department officers fire in the air at Kasarani police station in Nairobi when an officer in charge refuses to detain an innocent motorist.
- Anti-riot police arrest and lock in cells Kitui Central member of parliament Kaluki Nguli after she punches a district officer.
- The government unveils radical tax reform measures entailing the lowering of income tax and import duties in an attempt to speed up the country's industrialisation process.
- Three traffic policemen are foiled in their quest for 500 shillings as a "Christmas gift" from each motorist on the Thika-Murang'a road.
- Some doctors are allegedly diluting and adulterating the Pearl Omega drug before selling it to unsuspecting AIDS patients, its inventor Professor Arthur Obel says.
- A former jailbird caught stealing chicken is stoned to death by irate citizens who later burn his body.
- Kenya's third international airport at Eldoret is ready to start opertions and only awaits a decision from the Kenya Airport Authority. ($1=56 Kenyan shillings)
